goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/index.ts: every import(...) call is evaluated eagerly at module load, so all 29 app modules still load on first import of appStore; the map should hold thunks (() => import(...)) invoked by callers to achieve real lazy loading

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/index.ts the appStore object literal is constructed with values like `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`. Those `import(...)` expressions are executed immediately when index.ts is evaluated, which starts loading all listed modules at first import of `appStore` (each property becomes an already-in-flight Promise). So this change does not provide true per-app lazy loading; to defer loading until access, the map would need to store thunks (e.g., `() => import(...)`) or a Proxy/getter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125: forEach(async ...) pattern means the enclosing try/catch cannot catch failures from getCalendar/deleteEvent and the function returns before deletions complete

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts the diff changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { ... })` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })`. `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await the async callback, so the enclosing `try { ... } catch { ... }` will not catch rejections/errors from `await getCalendar(...)` or from the returned `deleteEvent(...)` promise. Additionally, the surrounding `Reschedule` function will continue execution past the `forEach` without waiting for deletions to finish, potentially completing/returning before integrations are actually deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125: forEach(async ...) pattern lets errors escape the try/catch as unhandled rejections and work is not awaited

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts the diff changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { ... })` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` inside a `try { ... } catch { ... }`. `Array.forEach` does not await the async callback, so the surrounding try/catch will not catch exceptions/rejections thrown inside the async function, and the deletions may run after the try block completes (potentially leading to unhandled promise rejections and non-deterministic completion). This is a real correctness issue introduced by the change to async `getCalendar` usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:460: forEach(async (credential) => ...) now includes an await getCalendar(...) before the update loop, but the outer handler does not await these, so recurring-booking calendar updates may not finish before the response and errors are unhandled; should be for...of or Promise.all

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts that a `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... })` was introduced (around the referenced lines ~458-466). `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, and the returned Promises are neither collected nor awaited. That means the recurring-booking calendar update/delete work inside that callback can continue after the handler proceeds, and any thrown/rejected errors inside the callback will not be caught by surrounding synchronous try/catch and may become unhandled rejections. A `for...of` with `await` or `await Promise.all(credentials.map(async ...))` would be required to ensure completion/error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/index.ts: no test verifies that appStore modules are resolved lazily or that callers handle the promise-valued map; a type-level test would have caught the un-awaited getCalendar in getCalendarCredentials

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `appStore` entries to dynamic `import()` promises and makes `getCalendar` async. In `CalendarManager.getCalendarCredentials`, `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` is indeed now un-awaited, but within the diff the downstream consumer (`getConnectedCalendars`) was updated to `await item.calendar`, indicating this is intentional promise propagation rather than a clear defect. The proposed finding is primarily about missing tests (“no test verifies…”) and a hypothetical “type-level test” catching it; that is not a verifiable bug introduced by the diff, and the diff itself shows callers being adapted to handle the promise in at least the shown path.
